result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.clique_number()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the clique number (size of the maximum clique). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L9770-L9863){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.clique_number() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The clique number `ω(G)` is the size of the largest clique in the graph. This is a fundamental graph invariant used in graph theory and combinatorial optimization. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Size of the maximum clique. Returns `0` for empty graphs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called on a directed graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - time complexity: `O(3^(n/3))` in the worst case - only works on undirected graphs - determining the clique number is NP-hard - for a complete graph `K_n`, the clique number is `n` - for a bipartite graph, the clique number is at most `2` ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#be36ba00 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) graph.clique_number() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: A path's largest clique is just a single edge, since no three nodes form a triangle: ::: {#3bdba1af .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) graph.clique_number() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: An empty graph has clique number `0`: ::: {#676eb424 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.Graph(directed=False).clique_number() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 0 ``` ::: ::: A complete graph `K_n` always has clique number `n`: ::: {#e4a54f17 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_full_graph(n=7) graph.clique_number() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 7 ``` ::: ::: Bipartite graphs can never contain a triangle, so their clique number never exceeds `2`: ::: {#0d1e6c8a .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "C") .add_edge("A", "D") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("B", "D") ) graph.clique_number() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
